verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις πάλιν πολλοῦ ὄχλου ὄντος καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων τί φάγωσιν προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς λέγει αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: En ekeinais tais hēmerais palin pollou ochlou ontos kai mē echontōn ti phagōsin proskalesamenos tous mathētas legei autois
verses.literal: In those days the crowd once again became very large and they had nothing to eat Jesus called the disciples to Him and said
verses.literalPt: NAQUELES dias, havendo uma grande multidão, e não tendo quê comer, Jesus chamou a si os seus discípulos, e disse-lhes:

verses.original: Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν
verses.transliteration: Splanchnizomai epi ton ochlon hoti ēdē hēmerai treis prosmenousin moi kai ouk echousin ti phagōsin
verses.literal: I have compassion for this crowd because they have already been . . . with Me three days and have nothing to eat
verses.literalPt: Tenho compaixão da multidão, porque há já três dias que estão comigo, e não têm quê comer.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀπολύσω αὐτοὺς νήστεις εἰς οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκλυθήσονται ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καί τινες αὐτῶν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἥκασιν
verses.transliteration: kai ean apolysō autous nēsteis eis oikon autōn eklythēsontai en tē hodō kai tines autōn apo makrothen hēkasin
verses.literal: If I send them home hungry they will faint along the way For some of them have come a great distance
verses.literalPt: E, se os deixar ir em jejum, para suas casas, desfalecerão no caminho, porque alguns deles vieram de longe.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι Πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπ’ ἐρημίας
verses.transliteration: Kai apekrithēsan autō hoi mathētai autou hoti Pothen toutous dynēsetai tis hōde chortasai artōn ep’ erēmias
verses.literal: His disciples replied - Where in this desolate place . . . could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people
verses.literalPt: E os seus discípulos responderam-lhe: De onde poderá alguém satisfazê-los de pão aqui no deserto?

verses.original: Καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτούς Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἑπτά
verses.transliteration: Kai ērōta autous Posous echete artous Hoi de eipan Hepta
verses.literal: How many loaves do you have Jesus asked Seven - they replied
verses.literalPt: E perguntou-lhes: Quantos pães tendes? E disseram-lhe: Sete.

verses.original: Καὶ παραγγέλλει τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν καὶ παρέθηκαν τῷ ὄχλῳ
verses.transliteration: Kai parangellei tō ochlō anapesein epi tēs gēs kai labōn tous hepta artous eucharistēsas eklasen kai edidou tois mathētais autou hina paratithōsin kai parethēkan tō ochlō
verses.literal: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground Then He took the seven loaves gave thanks and broke them and gave them to His disciples to set before the people And they distributed them to the crowd
verses.literalPt: E ordenou à multidão que se assentasse no chão. E, tomando os sete pães, e tendo dado graças, partiu-os, e deu-os aos seus discípulos, para que os pusessem diante deles, e puseram-nos diante da multidão.

verses.original: καὶ εἶχον ἰχθύδια ὀλίγα καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτὰ εἶπεν καὶ ταῦτα παρατιθέναι
verses.transliteration: kai eichon ichthydia oliga kai eulogēsas auta eipen kai tauta paratithenai
verses.literal: They also had . . . a few small fish and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well
verses.literalPt: Tinham também alguns peixinhos; e, tendo dado graças, ordenou que também lhos pusessem diante.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν καὶ ἦραν περισσεύματα κλασμάτων ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας
verses.transliteration: Kai ephagon kai echortasthēsan kai ēran perisseumata klasmatōn hepta spyridas
verses.literal: The people ate and were satisfied and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over
verses.literalPt: E comeram, e saciaram-se; e dos pedaços que sobejaram levantaram sete cestos.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ ὡς τετρακισχίλιοι καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: ēsan de hōs tetrakischilioi kai apelysen autous
verses.literal: And about four thousand men were present And when Jesus had dismissed the crowd
verses.literalPt: E os que comeram eram quase quatro mil; e despediu-os.

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐμβὰς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά
verses.transliteration: Kai euthys embas eis to ploion meta tōn mathētōn autou ēlthen eis ta merē Dalmanoutha
verses.literal: He immediately got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha
verses.literalPt: E, entrando logo no barco, com os seus discípulos, foi para as partes de Dalmanuta.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν αὐτῷ ζητοῦντες παρ’ αὐτοῦ σημεῖον ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πειράζοντες αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Kai exēlthon hoi Pharisaioi kai ērxanto syzētein autō zētountes par’ autou sēmeion apo tou ouranou peirazontes auton
verses.literal: Then the Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven
verses.literalPt: E saíram os fariseus, e começaram a disputar com ele, pedindo-lhe, para o tentarem, um sinal do céu.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναστενάξας τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ λέγει Τί ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ζητεῖ σημεῖον ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν εἰ δοθήσεται τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ σημεῖον
verses.transliteration: Kai anastenaxas tō pneumati autou legei Ti hē genea hautē zētei sēmeion amēn legō hymin ei dothēsetai tē genea tautē sēmeion
verses.literal: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said Why does this generation demand a sign Truly I tell you no sign will be given to this generation
verses.literalPt: E, suspirando profundamente em seu espírito, disse: Por que pede esta geração um sinal? Em verdade vos digo que a esta geração não se dará sinal algum.

verses.original: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἐμβὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν
verses.transliteration: kai apheis autous palin embas apēlthen eis to peran
verses.literal: And He left them got back into the boat . . . and crossed to the other side
verses.literalPt: E, deixando-os, tornou a entrar no barco, e foi para o outro lado.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπελάθοντο λαβεῖν ἄρτους καὶ εἰ μὴ ἕνα ἄρτον οὐκ εἶχον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ
verses.transliteration: Kai epelathonto labein artous kai ei mē hena arton ouk eichon meth’ heautōn en tō ploiō
verses.literal: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread except for . . . one loaf they had with them in the boat
verses.literalPt: E eles se esqueceram de levar pão e, no barco, não tinham consigo senão um pão.

verses.original: καὶ διεστέλλετο αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὁρᾶτε βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῆς ζύμης Ἡρῴδου
verses.transliteration: kai diestelleto autois legōn Horate blepete apo tēs zymēs tōn Pharisaiōn kai tēs zymēs Hērōdou
verses.literal: Watch out He cautioned them Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and - of Herod
verses.literalPt: E ordenou-lhes, dizendo: Olhai, guardai-vos do fermento dos fariseus e do fermento de Herodes.

verses.original: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχουσιν
verses.transliteration: kai dielogizonto pros allēlous hoti artous ouk echousin
verses.literal: So they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread
verses.literalPt: E arrazoavam entre si, dizendo: É porque não temos pão.

verses.original: Καὶ γνοὺς λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί διαλογίζεσθε ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ συνίετε πεπωρωμένην ἔχετε τὴν καρδίαν ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai gnous legei autois Ti dialogizesthe hoti artous ouk echete oupō noeite oude syniete pepōrōmenēn echete tēn kardian hymōn
verses.literal: Aware of their conversation Jesus asked them Why are you debating about having no bread Do you still not see or understand Do you have . . . such hard hearts
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, conhecendo isto, disse-lhes: Para que arrazoais, que não tendes pão? não considerastes, nem compreendestes ainda? tendes ainda o vosso coração endurecido?

verses.original: Ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες οὐ βλέπετε καὶ ὦτα ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐ μνημονεύετε
verses.transliteration: Ophthalmous echontes ou blepete kai ōta echontes ouk akouete kai ou mnēmoneuete
verses.literal: Having eyes do you not see And having ears do you not hear And do you not remember
verses.literalPt: Tendo olhos, não vedes? e tendo ouvidos, não ouvis? e não vos lembrais,

verses.original: ὅτε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους ἔκλασα εἰς τοὺς πεντακισχιλίους πόσους κοφίνους κλασμάτων πλήρεις ἤρατε Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Δώδεκα
verses.transliteration: hote tous pente artous eklasa eis tous pentakischilious posous kophinous klasmatōn plēreis ērate Legousin autō Dōdeka
verses.literal: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand how many basketfuls . . . of broken pieces did you collect Twelve they answered
verses.literalPt: Quando parti os cinco pães entre os cinco mil, quantas alcofas cheias de pedaços levantastes? Disseram-lhe: Doze.

verses.original: Ὅτε καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ εἰς τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους πόσων σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων ἤρατε Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἑπτά
verses.transliteration: Hote kai tous hepta eis tous tetrakischilious posōn spyridōn plērōmata klasmatōn ērate Kai legousin autō Hepta
verses.literal: And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand how many basketfuls . . . of broken pieces did you collect Seven they said
verses.literalPt: E, quando parti os sete entre os quatro mil, quantos cestos cheios de pedaços levantastes? E disseram-lhe: Sete.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Οὔπω συνίετε
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Oupō syniete
verses.literal: Then He asked them Do you still not understand
verses.literalPt: E ele lhes disse: Como não entendeis ainda?

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Βηθσαϊδάν Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ τυφλὸν καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψηται
verses.transliteration: Kai erchontai eis Bēthsaidan Kai pherousin autō typhlon kai parakalousin auton hina autou hapsētai
verses.literal: When they arrived at Bethsaida some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him
verses.literalPt: E chegou a Betsaida; e trouxeram-lhe um cego, e rogaram-lhe que o tocasse.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ἐξήνεγκεν αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς κώμης καὶ πτύσας εἰς τὰ ὄμματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν Εἴ τι βλέπεις
verses.transliteration: kai epilabomenos tēs cheiros tou typhlou exēnenken auton exō tēs kōmēs kai ptysas eis ta ommata autou epitheis tas cheiras autō epērōta auton Ei ti blepeis
verses.literal: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him Can you see anything He asked
verses.literalPt: E, tomando o cego pela mão, levou-o para fora da aldeia; e, cuspindo-lhe nos olhos, e impondo-lhe as mãos, perguntou-lhe se via alguma coisa.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναβλέψας ἔλεγεν Βλέπω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὅτι ὡς δένδρα ὁρῶ περιπατοῦντας
verses.transliteration: Kai anablepsas elegen Blepō tous anthrōpous hoti hōs dendra horō peripatountas
verses.literal: The man looked up and said I can see the people but they look like trees walking around
verses.literalPt: E, levantando ele os olhos, disse: Vejo os homens; pois os vejo como árvores que andam.

verses.original: Εἶτα πάλιν ἐπέθηκεν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ διέβλεψεν καὶ ἀπεκατέστη καὶ ἐνέβλεπεν τηλαυγῶς ἅπαντα
verses.transliteration: Eita palin epethēken tas cheiras epi tous ophthalmous autou kai dieblepsen kai apekatestē kai eneblepen tēlaugōs hapanta
verses.literal: Once again . . . Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes and when he opened them his sight was restored and he could see everything clearly
verses.literalPt: Depois disto, tornou a pôr-lhe as mãos sobre os olhos, e fez olhar para cima: e ele ficou restaurado, e viu cada homem claramente.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ λέγων Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην εἰσέλθῃς
verses.transliteration: kai apesteilen auton eis oikon autou legōn Mēde eis tēn kōmēn eiselthēs
verses.literal: Jesus sent him home and said Do not go back into the village
verses.literalPt: E mandou-o para sua casa, dizendo: Nem entres na aldeia, nem o digas a ninguém na aldeia.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς κώμας Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐπηρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων αὐτοῖς Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι
verses.transliteration: Kai exēlthen ho Iēsous kai hoi mathētai autou eis tas kōmas Kaisareias tēs Philippou kai en tē hodō epērōta tous mathētas autou legōn autois Tina me legousin hoi anthrōpoi einai
verses.literal: Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi On the way He questioned His disciples - Who do people say I am
verses.literalPt: E saiu Jesus, e os seus discípulos, para as aldeias de Cesaréia de Filipe; e no caminho perguntou aos seus discípulos, dizendo: Quem dizem os homens que eu sou?

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι Ἰωάννην τὸν Βαπτιστήν καὶ ἄλλοι Ἠλίαν ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι εἷς τῶν προφητῶν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de eipan autō legontes hoti Iōannēn ton Baptistēn kai alloi Ēlian alloi de hoti heis tōn prophētōn
verses.literal: They replied . . . . . . Some say John the Baptist - others say Elijah and still others one of the prophets
verses.literalPt: E eles responderam: João o Batista; e outros: Elias; mas outros: Um dos profetas.

verses.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι Ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός
verses.transliteration: Kai autos epērōta autous Hymeis de tina me legete einai Apokritheis ho Petros legei autō Sy ei ho Christos
verses.literal: But what about you Jesus asked Who do you say I am Peter answered - You are the Christ
verses.literalPt: E ele lhes disse: Mas vós, quem dizeis que eu sou? E, respondendo Pedro, lhe disse: Tu és o Cristo.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai epetimēsen autois hina mēdeni legōsin peri autou
verses.literal: And Jesus warned them not to tell anyone . . . about Him
verses.literalPt: E admoestou-os, para que a ninguém dissessem aquilo dele.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστῆναι
verses.transliteration: Kai ērxato didaskein autous hoti dei ton Huion tou anthrōpou polla pathein kai apodokimasthēnai hypo tōn presbyterōn kai tōn archiereōn kai tōn grammateōn kai apoktanthēnai kai meta treis hēmeras anastēnai
verses.literal: Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders - chief priests and scribes and that He must be killed and after three days rise again
verses.literalPt: E começou a ensinar-lhes que importava que o Filho do homem padecesse muito, e que fosse rejeitado pelos anciãos e príncipes dos sacerdotes, e pelos escribas, e que fosse morto, mas que depois de três dias ressuscitaria.

verses.original: καὶ παρρησίᾳ τὸν λόγον ἐλάλει καὶ προσλαβόμενος ὁ Πέτρος αὐτὸν ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: kai parrēsia ton logon elalei kai proslabomenos ho Petros auton ērxato epitiman autō
verses.literal: He spoke this message quite frankly and Peter took Him aside . . . and began to rebuke Him
verses.literalPt: E dizia abertamente estas palavras. E Pedro o tomou à parte, e começou a repreendê-lo.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιστραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐπετίμησεν Πέτρῳ καὶ λέγει Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου Σατανᾶ ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: Ho de epistrapheis kai idōn tous mathētas autou epetimēsen Petrō kai legei Hypage opisō mou Satana hoti ou phroneis ta tou Theou alla ta tōn anthrōpōn
verses.literal: But Jesus turning and looking at His disciples rebuked Peter and said Get behind Me Satan For you do not have in mind the things of God but the things of men
verses.literalPt: Mas ele, virando-se, e olhando para os seus discípulos, repreendeu a Pedro, dizendo: Retira-te de diante de mim, Satanás; porque não compreendes as coisas que são de Deus, mas as que são dos homens.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι
verses.transliteration: Kai proskalesamenos ton ochlon syn tois mathētais autou eipen autois Ei tis thelei opisō mou elthein aparnēsasthō heauton kai aratō ton stauron autou kai akoloutheitō moi
verses.literal: Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples and He told them If anyone wants to come after Me he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me
verses.literalPt: E chamando a si a multidão, com os seus discípulos, disse-lhes: Se alguém quiser vir após mim, negue-se a si mesmo, e tome a sua cruz, e siga-me.

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσει τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου σώσει αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: hos gar ean thelē tēn psychēn autou sōsai apolesei autēn hos d’ an apolesei tēn psychēn autou heneken emou kai tou euangeliou sōsei autēn
verses.literal: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it but whoever . . . loses his life for My sake . . . and for the gospel will save it
verses.literalPt: Porque qualquer que quiser salvar a sua vida, perdê-la-á, mas, qualquer que perder a sua vida por amor de mim e do evangelho, esse a salvará.

verses.original: Τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἄνθρωπον κερδῆσαι τὸν κόσμον ὅλον καὶ ζημιωθῆναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ti gar ōphelei anthrōpon kerdēsai ton kosmon holon kai zēmiōthēnai tēn psychēn autou
verses.literal: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world yet forfeit his soul
verses.literalPt: Pois, que aproveitaria ao homem ganhar todo o mundo e perder a sua alma?

verses.original: τί γὰρ δοῖ ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: ti gar doi anthrōpos antallagma tēs psychēs autou
verses.literal: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul
verses.literalPt: Ou, que daria o homem pelo resgate da sua alma?

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ μοιχαλίδι καὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται αὐτὸν ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων
verses.transliteration: hos gar ean epaischynthē me kai tous emous logous en tē genea tautē tē moichalidi kai hamartōlō kai ho Huios tou anthrōpou epaischynthēsetai auton hotan elthē en tē doxē tou Patros autou meta tōn angelōn tōn hagiōn
verses.literal: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels
verses.literalPt: Porquanto, qualquer que, entre esta geração adúltera e pecadora, se envergonhar de mim e das minhas palavras, também o Filho do homem se envergonhará dele, quando vier na glória de seu Pai, com os santos anjos.
